children.name: Psophodes
children.description: A genus of medium-sized, crested passerines endemic to Australia, characterised by stout, wedge-shaped bills and loud, distinctive vocalisations. They are divided into two groups: the whipbirds, with a characteristic whip-crack song, and the wedgebills, with a softer, bubbling call. They inhabit dense undergrowth, where they forage on the ground for insects and seeds.

children.name: Psophodes olivaceus
children.description: The eastern whipbird (Psophodes olivaceus) is an insectivorous passerine bird native to the east coast of Australia.

children.name: Psophodes nigrogularis
children.description: The western whipbird (Psophodes nigrogularis) is a passerine bird found in several scattered populations in Southwest Australia.

children.name: Psophodes occidentalis
children.description: The chiming wedgebill (Psophodes occidentalis), sometimes referred to as chiming whipbird, is a species of bird in the family Psophodidae.

children.name: Psophodes cristatus
children.description: The chirruping wedgebill (Psophodes cristatus) is a medium-sized member of the genus Psophodes, which consists or four to five songbirds endemic to Australia.

children.name: Androphobus
children.description: A monotypic genus of whipbird-like bird found only in the highland forests of New Guinea. It was once considered a babbler but is now placed in the Psophodidae. Very little is known about its ecology and behaviour.

children.name: Androphobus viridis
children.description: The Papuan whipbird (Androphobus viridis) is a little-known and unobtrusive species of bird in the family Psophodidae.
